evidence: Turner’s first latta branch explicitly gives Awankari lattā clothes, Punjabi lattā rag, Kumaoni lātā/lattā/latā clothes and Hindi lattā tattered cloth. The Kathoriya and Haryanvi laṭ(t)ā responses match this cloth/rag family with regional retroflexion. The r-expanded lattara/latthara branches are not selected.

Turner gives Doda ṭalla clothes and Western Pahari ṭalo cloth, alongside Nepali ṭālo piece of cloth. The adjacent Dogri/Gujari tal(l)- survey responses fit this cloth family; the source dental spelling is preserved, so this is explicitly a regional lexical comparison rather than a claimed exact phonetic match.

Turner gives Bengali khādi small piece of cloth, Nepali khādi rough cloth and Hindi/Gujarati/Marathi khādī coarse cotton cloth in the first khadda branch. The Adivasi Oriya khɔdi cloth answer fits the eastern short form; the r-bearing khaddara branch is excluded. This comparative placement does not decide possible later diffusion of the cloth term.

Turner explicitly lists Oriya pathara stone under prastara. The survey pəthəṛə is the same regional form with the source’s central vowels and rhotic. The entry separately marks several Punjabi-mediated Hindi/Bihari forms as loans; that instruction is not extended to this explicitly listed Oriya reflex.

Turner gives Lahnda pathar and Sindhi patharu stone under prastara. Saraiki phatar matches that northwestern series with aspiration on the initial stop in this survey. This is a qualified regional comparison; it is not automatically treated as one of the Punjabi loans Turner specifically identifies elsewhere.

Turner explicitly records Western Pahari Kotgarhi pátthər and Jaunsari pāthar stone. Kullui pətəṛ matches this neighbouring prastara family, with reduced vowels and no aspiration marked in the survey; its exact phonetic development remains a comparative qualification.

Turner’s gaṭṭa piece family includes Punjabi gaṭṭ/gaṭṭā and, explicitly in the addenda, Western Pahari gɔṭṭɔ and gaṭi small stone/pebble. The Awankari, Pothwari and Gujari stone responses match that northwestern lexical family. i-vowel giṭṭ- forms and responses combining different words are excluded.
